On The 6th Of February, 2025
 Criminal Appeal No. 4325 of 2023
 Chhotu Dhurvey
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ghanshyam Sharma, Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Ajay Shukla, Public Prosecutor for respondent - St
 Order
Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Learned counsel for the appellant does not want to press I.A.No.12411/2024, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A.No.12411/2024, is dismissed as not pressed.
With the consent of learned counsel for parties, heard finally.

This appeal under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C., is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 23.02.2023, passed by learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, Dindori, District Dindori (M.P.), in S.T.No.35/2020, whereby,
present appellant has been convicted for offence under Section 376 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5673 2 CRA-4325-2023 and fine of Rs.1,000/-, with default stipulation.
2. It is submitted that it is a case of consent, which has been converted into that of violation of privacy of the prosecutrix.
3. It is submitted that age of the prosecutrix is not proved.

Reading from the evidence of father of the prosecutrix (PW/2), it is submitted that father of the prosecutrix admitted in his examination in Chhotu Dhurvey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102922536/
1 chief that age of the prosecutrix is 23 years.

sentences.text: 4. Prosecutrix (PW/2), has stated that she was residing with her 'Bua' and on account of a dispute with her 'Bua' accused persons had also entered into an altercation, as a result of which, she had lodged a report of threat for death in the police station.
She had given application (Ex.P/2), as per the dictates of the police personnel, when police personnel recorded FIR (Ex.P/3).
She further stated that police personnel had not read over the report to her and sent her for medical examination to District Hospital Dindori.
5. In her examination in chief, this prosecutrix had stated that her age is 23 years.
She denied a suggestion that Chhotu Dhurve had taken her to 'Bashram' bushes and had performed any act of violation of her privacy.
She denied her statement with which she was confronted to have been given to the police personnel.
6. Yashoda Saiyam (PW/5), is the school teacher, who has exhibited Ex.P/14, which is 'Dakhil Kharij' register of the year 2009.

7. In this ' Dakhil Kharij' register, contention of this witness NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:5673 3 CRA-4325-2023 Yashoda Saiyam (PW/5), is that date of birth was not given by any of the parents of the victim, nor they had produced any document, but she had mentioned it after obtaining record of date of birth from the concerned Anganwadi, but unfortunately, no such record is available on record of this Court to show that any Anganwadi record was available to record date of birth of the prosecutrix as 06.01.2004.
8.
Dr. Kamlesh Raj (PW/4), has stated that no definite opinion could have been given about the immediate intercourse.
She further stated that no signs of forceful intercourse were found during the medical examination.

Dr. Kamlesh Raj (PW/4), has also stated that prosecutrix was advised to undergo X-ray for age determination and has admitted in cross-examination that age of the prosecutrix can be more than 16 years.

9. On perusal of the record, it is evident that Ex.P/12 referred to by the concerned Dr. Kamlesh Raj (PW/4), does not make mention of the X-ray report as to what was the age detected upon performance of radiological examination.
10.
Similarly, Ex.P/13, is also silent on this aspect.
Therefore, it is evident that there is no documentary evidence in regard to determination of age.

11. Apex Court in case of Birad Mal Singhvi Vs. Anand Purohit (AIR 1988 SC 1796), has noted in para 14 as under :-
"14.

entities.text: Birad Mal Singhvi Vs. Anand Purohit (AIR 1988 SC 1796)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If the entry in the scholar's register regarding date of birth is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5673 4 CRA-4325-2023 made on the basis of information given by parents, the entry would have evidentiary value but if it is given by a stranger or by someone else who had no special means of knowledge of the date Chhotu Dhurvey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102922536/
2 of birth, such an entry will have no evidentiary value.

entities.text: Chhotu Dhurvey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Merely because the documents such as extract of school register, mark list or certificate of Education Board etc. are proved, it does not mean that the contents of the documents are also proved.
Mere proof of such documents would not tantamount to proof of all the contents or the correctness of date of birth stated in the documents."

12. When this judgment of Apex Court is taken into consideration, then prosecution has failed to prove that the age of the victim was less than 18 years and in fact, all the witnesses, prosecutrix, her father and doctor have stated that age of the prosecutrix could have been more than 16years.
13. In fact, father of prosecutrix (PW/1) and prosecutrix (P/2), have stated the age of the prosecutrix to be 23 years.

School Teacher (PW/5), could not prove the date of birth by producing any record from the Anganwadi on the basis of which date of birth of prosecutrix was recorded in the school register Ex.P/14C and, therefore, prosecution having failed to prove the date of birth of the prosecutrix to show that she was minor, will not attract the provisions of Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act.
Therefore, when tested in the above light, then impugned judgment of conviction cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
It is set NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5673 5 CRA-4325-2023 aside.
14. Appeal is allowed and disposed off.
Appellant, if not required in any other case, be released forthwith.
Case property be disposed of in terms of the judgment of the trial Court.
15. Record of the trial Court be sent back immediately.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (ANURADHA S  JUDGE JUDGE  A.Praj.
